newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Liquidity keeps Manila call money at 10.53125 pct.
newsitem.headline: Liquidity keeps Manila call money at 10.53125 pct.

text.p: * T-bill traders cautious ahead of weekly auction
Philippine overnight money rate stayed unchanged at 10.53125 percent in a quiet session because the system was still awash with cash, traders said.
"Banks are still swamped with cash. Many banks were either lending overnight money to Central Bank or investing in short-term reverse repos," one trader said.
Banks are still grappling with influx of fresh funds from the cut in their reserve requirements and maturing reverse repos earlier this month.
Turnover in the interbank call market reached only 9.112 billion pesos ranging from 10.53125 percent to 10.5625 percent.
One trader said banks were already parking their excess funds in short-term reverse repos which offer better rates than Treasury bills.
The Central Bank was offering one-month reverse repos at 10.75 percent, two-month reverse repos at 10.875 percent and three-month reverse repos at 11.0 percent.
"These are good rates, especially when the market is still uncertain on how the T-bill rates will go today," he said.
Traders were cautious in trading their T-bills with little spreads. Most traders were expecting rates to move sideways with a 5.0 to 10 basis point downward bias.
Three-month bills were being bid between 10.725 percent and 11.80 and offered at 10.65 to 10.72 percent.

Six-month bills were being bought between 11.10 and 11.20, and sold between 11.00 to 11.05 percent. One-year bills were being bid between 11.40 and 11.50, while offered between 11.30 to 11.40 percent. - RAMONCITO DELA CRUZ 632 8418938 Fax 8176267
